citations.quote: The FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC directive may be specified only between clauses in divisions other than the procedure division
The FLAG-02 directive may be specified only between clauses in divisions other than the procedure division

cases.reason: FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC exists in 2002 only (2023 has no such directive, so there is no pointer). At --std 2002 the directive WORD is recognized and ignored: the construct row tests/version-matrix/constructs/flag-native-arithmetic-directive-window.json has a Text operand and no processor (kb/Work PB5600). SR1 is a placement rule. At --std 2002 the directive written inside a MOVE statement (fna-in-statement.cob) and inside a VALUE clause (fna-inside-clause.cob) compiles with no diagnostic. The compiler implements this very rule for FLAG-02/FLAG-14 (DirectivePlacementPass, COBOL2344: flag02-in-statement.cob and flag02-inside-clause.cob draw it at --std 2023), but the FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC and FLAG-85 construct rows carry no directivePlacement, so the pass never judges them. Sibling: §2002:7.2.11.2 SR1 (FLAG-85; flag85-in-statement.cob also silent at 2002). Not PB5600 (trailing text, flagging) nor PB5599 (word table).

citations.quote: No exception-name shall be specified more than once in one TURN directive
No exception-name-1 and file-name-1 combination shall be specified more than once in a TURN directive

cases.reason: 2002 forbids naming an exception-name twice in one directive whatever file-names follow it; 2023 (which merged 2002 SR3 and SR4) forbids only a repeated name/file combination. So '>>TURN EC-I-O F1 EC-I-O F2 CHECKING ON' violates 2002 SR3 and is legal in 2023. At --std 2002 the compiler accepts it (turn-dupname-files.cob): it applies the 2023 combination key at every edition. 'EC-SIZE EC-SIZE' and 'EC-I-O F1 EC-I-O F1' are refused (COBOL0718) at 2002.

cases.reason: The rule defers to the hierarchy of 2002 table 14 (14.5.12.1): the subordinates of a level-2 name are 2002's. 2002 EC-DATA has exactly EC-DATA-CONVERSION, -IMP, -INCOMPATIBLE, -PTR-NULL; 2023's EC-DATA adds EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE and EC-DATA-OVERFLOW (and EC-BOUND, EC-FLOW, EC-OO gain subordinates too). The compiler expands a level-2 name with its 2023 catalog at every edition, so the 2023 verdict does not show the 2002 expansion. Probe turn-data-float.cob: '>>TURN EC-DATA CHECKING ON', FLOAT-LONG 1.0E300 moved to FLOAT-SHORT; at --std 2002 the run unit terminates 'EC-DATA-OVERFLOW (fatal)' citing §2023:14.9.25.4, a condition that does not exist in 2002 and is not subordinate to EC-DATA there; control turn-control-float.cob (TURN EC-SIZE instead) prints [SURVIVED]. Compiler at 2002: wrong (also: 2023 defines EC-DATA-OVERFLOW only for standard floating-point usages, which FLOAT-SHORT is not). Same root as the reader's SR-7.2.19.2-2 finding (ExceptionCatalog entries with no introducing edition).
